Check rules
  • If a prize shows 3×, enter 3. A blank counts as 1×. Skip the top-left square.
  • The small numbers in the corners are score weights. Starting at , the check adds each entered multiplier minus 1, times that square’s weight.
Enter bet size

Check rules
  • Use the same units for the bet and coin values. For example, a 1.60 coin on a 0.80 bet counts as 2 bets. Empty cells count as zero.
  • Only the bottom two rows count. A wheel appears as a dot and adds when it’s in one of those rows. Use + Row to record a row above them.
  • 100× symbol. Judge the full board. The guide mentions the fifth position or higher as a rough reference.
  • 200× symbol. The guide usually considers this enough on its own. Review the layout if the board is very weak and the symbol is in row 6 or 7, counting from the bottom.
  • For either symbol in the bottom two rows, enter its displayed value in the grid like any other coin.

Check rules
  • Soft means one lower cutoff is met without an AP result. Leave any meter you want to skip blank. A blank counts as zero.
Enter values

Check rules
  • Use these rules for Ascending Fortunes and the original Stack Up Pays. Double Stack Up Pays uses different rules.
  • Skip the blue Mini. Leave any meter you want to skip blank. A blank counts as zero.
Enter reel counts

Check rules
  • Number the reels from left to right. If the machine shows 8 out of 10, choose 8.
  • Good through uses the current counts. Tap Next Spin when the machine advances, then update any reels that changed.

Enter spin and frames

For standard four-row versions with guaranteed wild conversion.

Guide rules
  • If the machine shows 8 out of 10, choose 8. Count reels from left to right and skip reel 5.
  • The five-row, exploding-scarab, jackpot, and non-guaranteed-wild versions use different rules.
  • One blank count is treated as zero. If both counts are zero, enter 0 in either field.
6+ touching empty frames
Guide cutoff

At 5, look for a second group of 5 or nearby empty frames that could connect. Fewer than 5 in the largest group is below the cutoff.

4× is borderline
Above 4× meets the cutoff

The guide cutoff includes exactly 4×. Recheck the multiplier whenever you switch bet levels.

2+ gold symbols
In the 3×2 grid

The cutoff applies at any spin count. Skip silver symbols and check each bet and denomination separately. The single-row Hold N Gold version uses a separate check.

Wild in positions 2–5
Count from the left

A stored wild in any of those spots qualifies. Each spin moves it one spot left. A wild already in the far-left spot disappears on the next spin.

  • Minor, Maxi, Major or Grand One filled spot qualifies on spins 1 through 9.
  • Mini One filled spot qualifies with four or fewer spins left. Look for 6–9 out of 10 on the display. Earlier, also look for a strong wild layout.
  • 10 out of 10 The next spin starts a fresh cycle.
What counts as a strong wild layout?

Look for existing wild spots that already form multiple three-of-a-kind ways or several four-of-a-kind ways or better. Read the reels from left to right and give less weight to layouts with a gap of two empty reels.

These are the guide’s estimates for a middle-return setup. The three middle bet levels were extrapolated.

Reading the bet level

Use the multiplier on the bet button. For example, if the 1× button is 50 credits, the 150-credit button is 3×. A bet button can start a spin when the machine has enough credits.

The author tested 1× and 10× directly and estimated the three middle cutoffs.

Reading the bet level

Use the multiplier within the chosen denomination. For example, if 1× is 100 credits, the 300-credit button is 3×. Check the 1,800 counter at that bet level.

Active wild column
At least 1 coin above it

An empty coin holder means the wild column has expired. The guide treats a wild on reel 3 without a 2× as a thinner setup.

3+ Wild bubbles
Below the top row

Count the bubbles labeled Wild. They move up one row per spin, so the top row leaves play on the next spin. Jackpot bubbles belong to a separate feature.

Use the three-number Bubble Boost edition. The must-hit-by limits are 60 for Lagoon, 50 for Ocean, and 60 for Reef. The guide uses the same cutoffs with the boost on or off.

Around $900
Review estimate

Read the Minor Platinum meter with the $1,000 limit. The guide gives different estimates for different setups.

Check rules
  • The chart uses $900 at a lower-return setup and about $890 at a higher-return setup.
  • The written examples give $895 and $900 respectively. Use the chart as a review cue.
  • The illustrated bet range is $3.75 to $7.50 at the minimum bets for 5¢ and 10¢.
11+ on Spins
Review · thin at 11

Read the counter labeled Spins on the gold pot. The guide considers 11 thin and generally skips this game.

Check rules

The guide estimates little added value past about 17 spins on the counter. Much of the result depends on the final multiplier.

Shaking center pillar
Gold dragon behind it

Check the three center pillars at the selected bet. Any green-orb count can qualify while at least one of those pillars is shaking with the dragon visible.

Check rules

Recheck as the pillars change. Stop when none of the center pillars are both shaking and backed by a gold dragon. A bet button can start a spin when the machine has enough credits.

Check the prize tier
Secondhand estimates
  • Second tier or higher Look for a large gem or crown on the coin table. The guide singles out the emerald.
  • Red + blue One of each with at least one coin column.
  • Two blues With a colored bracelet and at least three coin columns.
  • One blue With a Free Games bracelet and at least three coin columns.
Check rules

For the one-blue route, look for the Free Games bracelet. The +2 Pushes piece is a separate award. The chart leaves pearls and small reds out of these combinations.
